application: Standalone educational example, not part of H.E.R.B.I.E. V1 robot BOM or CAD
open_measurements: actual emitter and receiver housing diameters
actual LED and optical detector model and spectral response
actual component dimensions and mounting interface
physical beam height and alignment distance
battery polarity and LED current limiter
ESP32-C3 board revision and ADC-capable pinout
light sensor divider minimum and maximum input voltage
wire strain relief, enclosure wall thickness and print fit

parts.name: Emitter stand
parts.function: Holds the emitter steady and below eye level.
parts.salvage_candidate: Cardboard support, clamp or stable recycled base.
parts.verification_needed: Measure beam height, stability and alignment.

parts.name: Emitter housing
parts.function: Protects and aims the light. An intact flashlight can replace this whole set of DIY emitter parts.
parts.salvage_candidate: Low-brightness battery flashlight or toy enclosure.
parts.verification_needed: Measure actual housing size and safe beam spread.

parts.name: Emitter batteries / holder
parts.function: Supplies the light emitter independently of the receiver.
parts.salvage_candidate: Intact low-voltage battery compartment from a toy.
parts.verification_needed: Confirm supply polarity, voltage and cell condition.

parts.name: Emitter switch
parts.function: Convenient on/off switch; often already part of a flashlight.
parts.salvage_candidate: Battery toy or holiday light switch.

parts.name: LED current limiter
parts.function: A bare LED requires correctly designed current limiting. A complete rated flashlight may already include this.
parts.verification_needed: Calculate and measure LED current before sustained operation.

parts.name: Diffused visible LED
parts.function: Emits a low-brightness visible beam toward the sensor. No laser required.
parts.salvage_candidate: Diffused low-power toy LED or complete dim flashlight.
parts.verification_needed: Avoid looking into the source; mount below eye height.

parts.name: Receiver stand
parts.function: Keeps the receiving sensor aligned with the emitter.
parts.salvage_candidate: Reused cardboard, clip or adjustable stand.

parts.name: Black sensor tube
parts.function: Shades the sensor from room light and improves directionality.
parts.salvage_candidate: Short black straw or light-proof small tube.
parts.verification_needed: Compare sensor response with/without room lighting.

parts.name: Light detector
parts.function: A photoresistor or phototransistor senses the light. This model depicts an LDR.
parts.salvage_candidate: Identified low-voltage light-reactive toy or purchased LDR.

parts.name: Sensor bias / resistor
parts.function: For a bare LDR, a resistor divider creates a safe analog voltage. Sensor modules may include it.
parts.verification_needed: Check voltage is always within chosen ESP32 ADC limits.

parts.name: Receiver housing
parts.function: Holds and protects the sensor wiring. Dimensions are unknown until parts are measured.
parts.verification_needed: Check fit and cable exit clearance.

parts.name: ESP32-C3 controller
parts.function: Reads the sensor voltage through an appropriate GPIO/ADC pin and can host a Wi-Fi alarm page.
parts.salvage_candidate: Usually easier to buy a known, inexpensive development board.
parts.verification_needed: Confirm exact pinout and 3.3 V GPIO requirements.

parts.name: USB power supply
parts.function: A correctly rated USB power bank powers the ESP32. The emitter uses separate batteries.
parts.salvage_candidate: Existing USB power bank and matching cable.
parts.verification_needed: Check board input requirements, cable and power-bank auto-off.
